text.p: A French Open already rich in incident lost both its defending champions within the space of two hours on Tuesday as Steffi Graf and Yevgeny Kafelnikov discovered that titles are not regained by reputation alone.

Graf's magnificent run at Roland Garros, which has seen her reach the semifinals every year for the past decade, was finally ended by South African Amanda Coetzer, whose 6-1 6-4 victory offered further evidence the German champion is no longer the force she used to be.

Kafelnikov, who like Graf has missed three months of the year with injury, found himself swept away by the irresistible strokeplay of 20-year-old Brazilian Gustavo Kuerten, who now finds himself facing Belgium's Filip Dewulf in a grand slam semifinal which seemed barely credible even three days ago.
Barring the Eiffel Tower falling over, little else that happens this week can possibly surprise Parisian tennis fans, but Kuerten's 6-2 5-7 2-6 6-0 6-4 victory was fully deserved and no fluke.

Before accounting for the Russian world number three, Kuerten had already overcome clay specialists Thomas Muster and Andrei Medvedev in five sets and his world ranking of 66 does not do justice to a genuine talent with confidence to match.

"My wins against Muster and Medvededev boosted my confidence and I said to myself 'Why not Kafelnikov?'," revealed the effervescent Kuerten, once again dressed in the blue-and-yellow kit which has failed to impress the organisers.
"I'm getting used to playing five sets. The only difference today is that for the first time I was two sets to one down."

Kafelnikov, supplied by the same clothing manufacturer, started the match in almost identical coloured gear to that of his opponent but soon discovered he would not be allowed the same playing freedom he enjoyed against Mark Philippoussis in his previous round.

"His ground strokes are really impressive. He was making shots from all angles of the court," said the Russian, who broke a finger on a punch-bag just before the Australian Open in January. "The key was the beginning of the fourth set when I lost my concentration and I never recovered from that."
So total was Kuerten's domination in that fourth set he allowed his opponent just eight points and, from the moment he broke again in the opening game of the fifth, he was able to call the shots.
The first Brazilian ever to reach the last four at a grand slam, Kuerten's only title came in a Challenger Series event in his native country last month.

He now faces Dewulf, the first qualifier since John McEnroe at Wimbledon in 1977 to reach a grand slam semifinal, and will not have been too concerned by the Belgian's display against Sweden's Magnus Norman on Tuesday.

Dewulf, the first man from his country in the last four at Roland Garros for 39 years, can be found in 122nd place on the computer but still managed to complete a 6-2 6-7 6-4 6-3 success seconds before rain swept across the stadium, causing the action on all courts to be interrupted briefly.

Norman had beaten world number one Pete Sampras en route to the last eight but had no answer to the Belgian's powerful forehand which accounted for Spanish eighth seed Alex Corretja in the previous round.
"If he keeps playing like that he has a good chance to win the tournament," Norman said. "I was more impressed with him than I was with Sampras."

Graf, who had been eyeing a sixth French title and her third in succession, blamed a lack of self-confidence for her demise and Coetzer, who beat the German 6-0 6-1 in Berlin last month, showed no mercy.
"She's not playing her best tennis right now," said Coetzer, seeded 11th. "You can sense that she lacks confidence. She's had some injury problems and maybe she's not 100 percent fit."

Graf, still wearing a bandage on the injured left knee which kept her out of action earlier this year, trailed 6-1 3-1 when rain interrupted play for some 30 minutes but could not find an escape route when the clouds lifted.

"I sat down during the break but I didn't manage to calm down," said Graf, who lost her temper on several occasions on court, swearing loudly in German. "I just couldn't find the positive attitude I needed."

More bad news for Graf came in the shape of Monica Seles's 3-6 6-2 7-5 win over Mary Joe Fernandez which is set to relegate the German to third place in the world rankings, the first time she has dropped out of the top two for a decade.
Coetzer will meet Croatia's Iva Majoli, a 6-3 5-7 6-2 winner over Romania's Ruxandra Dragomir, while Seles plays world number one Martina Hingis in the other women's semifinal on Thursday.
Hingis dismantled sixth seed and former French champion Arantxa Sanchez Vicario 6-2 6-2 and remains hot favourite to add the title to the Australian Open crown she has already collected this year.
